name: Probabilistic install matching (IP plus user agent)
plain: An MMP guesses which ad click led to an install by matching IP, device model and OS version within a short time window.
meaning: Without IDs, the vendor matches the click (IP, UA, language, OS) with the first app open from the same signals, usually within hours. Apple treats this as fingerprinting for ATT-denied users.

android.store_policy: Play does not ban it; used as fallback to referrer
android.api_surface: MMP click redirect + SDK first open
android.note: Used when Install Referrer is not available, e.g. non-Play installs.

ios.store_policy: App Review 5.1.2(i): fingerprinting prohibited for tracking; vendors limit it to non-user-level modeling
ios.note: iCloud Private Relay hides the Safari IP, breaking matches; Apple leaves enforcement to review.

limits.headline: Can guess which ad led to your install by matching your IP, phone model and timing
limits.user_action: You tap an ad, install the app, then open it within a short window
can: Match your ad click to your first open using IP, phone model and system version
Credit the right ad when no exact install code is available
Work for installs outside Google Play on Android and, with gaps, on iPhone
cannot: Match you for sure; it is a guess and can be wrong
Match you on a long delay; it needs a short time window
Match you on iPhone when iCloud Private Relay hides your Safari IP
See anything else about you from this step alone
limits.differs: Android has a reliable referrer for Play installs, so guessing is a backup. On iPhone it is often the main method, though Private Relay breaks it.

story.what_it_is: A guess about which ad led to an install, made by comparing network and device details.
story.for_you: You tap an ad, install the app and the ad firm quietly matches the two by network address and device details. You never see this. It can be wrong, especially on shared Wi-Fi.
story.for_makers: When IDs are blocked, ad firms still need to say which campaign worked. Matching in a short window gives an estimate for budgets. Apple treats it as fingerprinting when the person said no to tracking.

use_cases.example: A game studio checks which of five video ads brought a new player, using the click and first open from the same Wi-Fi.
A retailer measures whether an influencer link caused app installs.
A mobile game pays an ad network per install, and the match decides who gets paid.
Fraud teams spot clicks that claim installs by guessing from the same address at odd hours.
A booking app estimates which search ad led to its first booking in the app.
A marketing team compares the guess to Apple's own aggregate ad reports.

story.android_note: Allowed more freely, though Google Play rules limit ad use.
story.ios_note: Apple warns it counts as fingerprinting for people who tapped Ask App Not to Track.

technical_bounds: Accuracy falls with shared Wi-Fi, VPN, Private Relay
Not allowed on iOS for denied users per Apple

abuse: Joining a click to a device without consent

history.change: ATT: IP+UA matching not allowed for denied users; vendors restrict or rebrand
iCloud Private Relay hides Safari IP from apps' redirectors
